about.title: Clearlake Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls on someone else's property happen for reasons that are entirely preventable: wet floors near Lakeshore Drive businesses, uneven walkways at older buildings, broken stairs, poor lighting in parking areas off Olympic Drive, or spilled liquids left unattended in a store aisle. In Clearlake, where much of daily life runs through a handful of corridors like Rt 53 and Old Highway 53, a single bad fall at a gas station, grocery store, or apartment complex can sideline someone for weeks. California law requires the property owner to have known, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before you can hold them responsible. That's why what happens in the minutes and hours after your fall matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney from our network who can evaluate your fall, gather evidence, and explain your options, all on a contingency basis so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Fall Victims in Clearlake Reach Out to Us

items.title: We Understand the 'Notice' Requirement
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network can help identify witnesses, prior complaints, or maintenance records that speak to that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Clearlake businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be critical to supporting your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the fall — your share of fault simply reduces, rather than eliminates, potential compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Clearlake?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If a government-owned property was involved, such as a public sidewalk or building, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. Because these timelines are strict, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for my own fall?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your potential recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically barred. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your situation.

items.question: Are falls in Clearlake usually connected to specific locations?
items.answer: Public crash and injury data for Clearlake shows higher collision volumes along corridors like Rt 53, Lakeshore Drive, Old Highway 53, and Olympic Drive, often peaking on Friday afternoons — though that data reflects traffic collisions generally, not premises falls specifically. Slip and fall incidents can happen at any business, apartment complex, or rental property in town regardless of nearby traffic patterns. What matters most for your claim is documenting the specific hazard and location where you fell.
